sentences.text: 2 I am considering these two Writ Petitions together because the petitioner in both these cases is the same and the reliefs sought for therein, though not dependent on each other, are edificed on similar factual circumstances.

2. Both these Writ Petitions have been filed by Smt.K.K.Chadri, who alleges that the Panchayath is now attempting to evict her from the shop room leased out to her in the year 2013, without following law and in violation of the applicable Statutes and Regulations.

3. WP(C)No.24000/2015 has been filed by the petitioner impugning Ext.P10 decision taken by the Panchayath, as per which, its Secretary has informed her that they have decided to evict her from the shop room and to re-allot it to others through a public auction.

She says that Ext.P10 is untenable and that the Panchayath could not have taken such a decision WPC 24000/15 &
26043/19 because she can be evicted only as per the applicable Civil Law.

4. WP(C)No.26043//2019 was subsequently filed when the petitioner received Ext.P3 notice, as per which, she was asked to demolish certain alleged unauthorised constructions made to the shop room and she says that the allegations in this notice are untenable and without factual basis.

She,
therefore, prays that the said notice be set aside and she be allowed to continue with the occupation of the shop room without interdiction from the Panchayath.

5. In response, Sri.R.Parthasarathy, learned Standing Counsel for the Azhiyur Grama Panchayath,
submits that Ext.P10 in WP(C)No.24000/2015 is only a decision taken by the Panchayath to evict the petitioner in terms of law and to re-allot the shop room to others.

He says that the petitioner could not have WPC 24000/15 & 26043/19 challenged this decision because she cannot assert that no action be taken to evict her in terms of law or that the Panchayath cannot re- allot the shop room to other persons.
He, therefore, prays that liberty may be granted to his client to take appropriate action pursuant to Ext.P10 as per law.

6. Coming to Ext.P3 in WP(C)No.26043/2019, Sri.Parthasarthay submits that the said notice is only one issued under Section 235W of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act ((herein after referred to as 'the Act' for short) and that the petitioner can always answer the same, thus leading to a final order to be issued by the Secretary in terms of law.
He says, therefore, that this Writ Petition is not maintainable, since the petitioner cannot assert that an action under Section 235W cannot be even initiated against her.

7. I have considered the afore submissions WPC 24000/15 & 26043/19 and also examined the materials available on record.
8.
It is without doubt that the assertion of the petitioner is that she has been sought to be evicted by the Panchayath without following due procedure.

However, going by Ext.P10 in WP(C)No.24000/2015, the Panchayath has only taken a decision to evict her, which they can do only after following applicable law and after following the procedure as is mandated for such purpose.
I do not see why the petitioner should be threatened by Ext.P10, since she certainly can challenge any further proceedings initiated against her, if it is not done as per law.

sentences.text: Coming to Ext.P3 in WP(C)No.26043/2019 is concerned, as rightly pointed out by Sri.Parthasarathy

, the same is only a notice under Section 235W of the Act and obviously, therefore,
the petitioner can file her WPC 24000/15 & 26043/19 objections to the same, leading her to be heard by the Secretary of the Panchayath as per the said provisions, culminating in a final order under the said section.
Here again, I do not see why the petitioner should have any grievance against Ext.P3 since her rights or remedies are not, in any manner, trammelled by such proceedings.

In the afore circumstances, I order these writ petitions in the following manner:
a) WP(C)No.24000/2015 is dismissed;
however, clarifying that the Panchayath will seek eviction of the petitioner only as per law and after following due procedure, including by notifying her appropriately with respect to the procedure that they intend to adopt.
b) WP(C)No.26043/2019 is ordered, leaving liberty to the petitioner to file necessary objections against Ext.P3, based on which, the Secretary of the Panchayath will hear her WPC 24000/15 &
26043/19 leading to a final order under Section 235W of the Act, if it is so warranted; in which event, the petitioner will be left with all further remedies against the same, as she may be advised in law.
Sd/-
